title: CLIMASTRA
text:
Profile
Dr. Kumari Sweta is a Founder and Director of CLIMASTRA – Climate Strategy and Analytics. She is an earth scientist and geospatial professional with more than ten years of experience in disaster resilience, geohazard assessment and GIS, working with research institutions and government agencies including IIT Roorkee and the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).
Her PhD at IIT Roorkee brought earthquake shaking into landslide susceptibility assessment and produced empirical equations for estimating co-seismic slope displacement in the Northern Himalaya. She uses hazard and geospatial information for risk-informed planning, mitigation design and technical assessment, and brings experience in stakeholder coordination, technical reporting and training.

title: CLIMASTRA
text:
Areas of expertise

Landslide inventory, susceptibility zonation and risk assessment, including statistical and machine-learning models
Seismic hazard scenarios (probabilistic seismic hazard assessment) and co-seismic landslide displacement
Runout and debris-flow simulation (RAMMS) and slope stability analysis (GeoStudio, Plaxis)
Site prioritisation and slope stabilisation and mitigation planning, structural and non-structural
Remote sensing and GIS: hazard mapping, image processing, terrain modeling and data integration (ArcGIS, QGIS, ERDAS Imagine, Google Earth Engine, R-CRISIS)
Technical reporting, multi-stakeholder coordination, capacity building and training

title: CLIMASTRA
text:
Profile
Dr. Arshini Saikia advises CLIMASTRA on air quality, emissions and the health and climate impacts of air pollution. She is an atmospheric scientist with more than 10 years of experience in air quality modeling, emission inventories and science-to-policy support across South Asia and the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH).
She is a Post-Doctoral Research Scientist at the Laboratoire de Météorologie Dynamique (LMD), Institut Pierre-Simon Laplace (IPSL), École Polytechnique, France. There she compares and harmonizes gridded emission inventories (EDGAR, CAMS, GFED, APIFLAME) for black carbon, organic carbon, CO, NOx and NH₃ over South and Southeast Asia, and assesses ozone- and methane-attributable mortality and crop losses across HKH countries. Previously, as Air Quality Modelling Analyst at ICIMOD (2023–2026), she led the operational air quality forecast for the HKH region and co-developed a regional air quality dashboard with NASA SERVIR. That work supported monitoring and clean-air action with the governments of Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and India.

title: CLIMASTRA
text:
Profile
Prof. Chandra Shekhar Prasad Ojha advises CLIMASTRA on dam safety and hydrology. He is a Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee, specializing in hydraulics engineering, and holds the Indian National Academy of Engineering (INAE) Chair Professorship (2026–2028).
He was Head of the Department of Civil Engineering at IIT Roorkee (2015–2019) and has held the AS Arya Institute Chair and Institute Chair professorships there. Internationally, he has been an Adjunct Professor at the University of Missouri, the Curtis Visiting Professor at Purdue University, a Royal Academy of Engineering Distinguished Visiting Fellow (U.K.) and an Alexander von Humboldt Research Fellow. He chairs the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Sectional Committee on Glacial Lake Outburst Floods and Landslide Lake Outburst Floods, and is Chief Editor of the Journal of the Indian Water Resources Society.

title: CLIMASTRA
text:
Profile
Dr. Praveen Kumar Singh is a Founder and Director of CLIMASTRA – Climate Strategy and Analytics. He is an atmospheric scientist working on black carbon, air quality, climate and the cryosphere of the Hindu Kush Himalaya and South Asia, and is currently a Postdoctoral Research Scientist at the Laboratoire de Météorologie Dynamique (LMD-IPSL/CNRS), École Polytechnique, France, studying pollutants, meteorology and climate in South and Southeast Asia.
His career spans in-situ aerosol measurements, atmospheric remote sensing and glacier energy- and mass-balance modeling at IIT Roorkee and ICIMOD (Kathmandu), and air-quality policy as Senior Program Associate at WRI India, where he advised the Gorakhpur city administration. In 2019 he was a science team member of the National Geographic and Rolex Perpetual Planet Everest Expedition, measuring light-absorbing impurities in snow and ice at Everest Base Camp.

title: CLIMASTRA
text:
Profile
Rajeev Ranjan is the Founder and Director of CLIMASTRA – Climate Strategy and Analytics. He is a geospatial professional with 8 years of experience working with leading research and technical institutions (IIT Roorkee, IIRS Dehradun and NIH Roorkee) and in industry at Spatial Decisions, New Delhi.
He has submitted his PhD thesis at IIT Roorkee on glacial lake mapping and flow simulation in selected Himalayan watersheds. As a Senior Research Fellow at IIT Roorkee’s Centre of Excellence in Disaster Mitigation and Management, he models how future climate change will affect Himalayan snow- and glacier-melt runoff, using hydrological models driven by CMIP6 climate projections. His earlier work covers river morphology of the Rapti, Sharda and Ganga, field and laboratory snow spectroscopy, and landslide susceptibility and debris-flow modeling in Uttarakhand.
